Users can convert any photo into iMessage or WhatsApp stickers, or create custom sticker packs inspired by images. Details below.

「Turn any photo, idea, or inside joke into a custom sticker pack」

A few days ago, data discovered in code revealed that OpenAI is developing a feature that lets users create custom stickers in ChatGPT and export them directly to WhatsApp.

OpenAI officially announced the feature today, stating that it supports both iMessage and WhatsApp, and can produce images with transparent backgrounds.

Below is OpenAI's announcement:

With the new feature, users can upload one or more images from their photo library, then ask ChatGPT to convert each image into stickers, remix them into multiple stickers, or add or remove elements.

Users can also transfer a style from another image, or simply describe the desired style directly in the prompt.

Once the stickers are ready, users can click the "Add to chat apps" button to export them to supported messaging apps. Current options include:

iMessage, WhatsApp (minimum 3 stickers required for export), Save to Photos

It's worth noting that WhatsApp's requirement of at least three stickers is a Meta-side requirement, not a ChatGPT limitation.

When we tested it, simply uploading one image and entering the prompt "Create an iMessage sticker" was enough to generate an asset with a transparent background—it could even extend the frame outward, restoring the top of the subject's head that had been cropped out of the original image.

After selecting "iMessage" from the "Add to chat apps" menu, the sticker appears in a dedicated ChatGPT section within the Stickers carousel of the Messages app.
